How much do real estate agents make in Holly Hill?

There’s no salary. Agents earn a commission on each sale, so income scales with how much you sell. The math: each deal pays the sale price × the commission rate × your side of the deal (usually 50%) × your brokerage split. Multiply by the number of deals you close in a year and you have your gross. The calculator above assumes a 50% side. Adjust the other numbers to your situation.

What moves the number most in Holly Hill?

Two levers dominate: volume (more closings) and price point (higher-value markets). The Volusia County median, which covers Holly Hill, is about $343,000, and roughly 900 homes sell each month countywide, so the volume is there for an agent who can find clients. Holly Hill itself tends to run more affordably than that county median, which means more first-time and value-conscious buyers to work with, and a wider pipeline for an agent building a book from scratch.

What the estimate doesn’t include

This is a gross figure. Out of it come brokerage fees, the marketing you pay for, MLS and board dues, and self-employment taxes. That’s exactly why a new agent’s real take-home depends so much on the brokerage: one that includes marketing and tools and helps you get clients faster can mean more closings and lower costs than a higher split where you fund everything. See how to become a real estate agent in Holly Hill.

This estimator is a simplified gross projection and not a guarantee of income. It ignores fees, taxes, and market variation. Educational only, not financial advice.

faq.q: How much do real estate agents make in Holly Hill?
faq.a: It varies widely because income is commission-based. As a rough estimate, multiply deals per year by average sale price, the commission rate, your side of the deal (usually 50%), and your brokerage split. At the ~$343,000 Volusia County median, 12 deals a year at 5% total, a 50% side, and a 70% split is about $72,000 gross before fees and taxes.

faq.q: Do real estate agents get a salary in Holly Hill?
faq.a: No. Almost all Holly Hill real estate agents are independent contractors paid by commission on each closed sale, not a salary. Income depends entirely on production.

faq.q: How can a new agent in Holly Hill increase their first-year income?
faq.a: Close more deals, faster. That comes from training, lead and marketing support, and a recognized brand, which is why the brokerage you join matters more than the headline split in year one.
